correctness.rationale: The outer-product parametrization is bijective after projective normalization. The three nonzero/zero cases are exhaustive. When both cross-evaluations are nonzero the bracket is invertible on its two-dimensional image, forcing the two-eigenline semisimple type even in characteristic two. Counting the eligible projective lines and nonzero covectors gives the zero and rank-one fibers. For each admissible rank-two target, \(q-1\) scalar choices for each ordered eigenline pair produce all witnesses; the two characteristics yield 2 or \(q(q+1)\) eigenline pairs. Global pair mass and all-target finite checks corroborate every boundary including \(n=2\) and characteristic two. The infinite claim is algebraically proved, not inferred from finite samples.

value.rationale: The minimal nonzero nilpotent conjugacy class and the Lie bracket are canonical, so exact prescribed-target bracket multiplicity and image support are natural structural invariants. The theorem resolves the entire map, not an arbitrarily sliced datum, across all dimensions and all finite fields. It exhibits a characteristic-two eigenline collapse with a \(q(q^2-1)\) rank-two fiber versus \(2(q-1)\) in odd characteristic, supplies the zero and rank-one strata, and exact image cardinalities; these are not consequences of the known geometric existence statements alone.
